_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES USED: render indices 2, 4, 6 ONLY (= printed Pages 3, 5, 7 of 8). Every one of the 8 indices is accounted for: idx0 = bilingual cover (Hindi bullets above English bullets, no questions, 'Page 1 of 8'); idx1 = HINDI General Instructions + Section A Q1-6; idx2 = ENGLISH General Instructions + Section A Q1-6; idx3 = HINDI Section B Q7-10 + Section C header + Q11-12; idx4 = ENGLISH Section B Q7-10 + Section C header + Q11-12; idx5 = HINDI Q13 + Q14 case study; idx6 = ENGLISH Q13 + Q14 case study; idx7 = BLANK (printed 'Page 8 of 8', carries only QR codes, the 310 A code and the footer). The alternating hypothesis HELD EXACTLY and the three documented failure modes were checked for and did NOT occur: I read the top of every odd page and the last page, and NONE carried English overflow — each language block is laid out as a self-contained mirrored page rather than a continuous flow, so no question straddles a language boundary; there is no English-only final page (idx7 is blank); and there is no mid-paper parity inversion (the Hindi and English blocks occupy exactly 3 pages each). Question numbers run 1 to 14 unbroken with every sub-part present. STRUCTURE CONFIRMED off idx2 and the cover: 14 questions, 40 marks, 2 hours; Section A Q1-6 @2 = 12, Section B Q7-10 @3 = 12, Section C Q11-14 @4 = 16; Q14 is a case study with 2 sub-parts of 2 marks each. NO MCQs ANYWHERE — every row is subjective, so there are no options, no answer letters, and the blind MCQ key re-derivation that anchors 2023-2026 does not apply to this paper. INTERNAL CHOICE: instruction (vi) reads only 'There is an internal choice in some questions' and prints NO counts, so the four OR-alternatives (Q6, Q8, Q9, Q12) were found by reading the paper and then CONFIRMED question-by-question against the marking scheme, which reprints both branches — the scheme prints an OR block for exactly Q6, Q8, Q9 and Q12 and for no other question. The 40-mark sum is structurally blind to a missed alternative, so it was not used as the check. All 11 marking-scheme pages are likewise accounted for: ms p00-p01 are the examiner's general instructions (items 1-17, no question content), ms p02-p10 are the scheme proper, running Q1 to Q14 and closing with '* * *'. THE PLANE: Q4 (distance of a point from a plane) and Q13 (line meets plane) are filed on 'The Plane', the subtopic added to the live Three Dimensional Geometry axis on 2026-08-19 for exactly this 2022 Term-2 need — rationalised NCERT Ch.11 dropped the plane, so the textbook ingest that defined this axis had created no such subtopic. Both were first filed on the closest available subtopic with a mismatch flag; the flags are removed because the gap they named is resolved. No solutions written: this pipeline authors them later from the marking scheme. TYPOGRAPHY NOTE: the paper is inconsistent about italicising variables — it sets x and lambda italic but y and z upright roman in Q4, Q8, Q10 and Q11. That is typesetting, not mathematics, and is normalised to ordinary LaTeX italics throughout.

questions.stem: Find the general solution of the differential equation : \(e^{dy/dx} = x^2\).

Write the projection of the vector \((\vec{b} + \vec{c})\) on the vector \(\vec{a}\), where \(\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}\), \(\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{c} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 4\hat{k}\).
If the distance of the point (1, 1, 1) from the plane \(x - y + z + \lambda = 0\) is \(\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{3}}\), find the value(s) of \(\lambda\).
Two cards are drawn successively with replacement from a well shuffled pack of 52 cards. Find the probability distribution of the number of spade cards.

questions._flag: PRINTED AS 'atleast' (one word) — transcribed as printed, not silently corrected to 'at least'. The same paper's Hindi block carries no equivalent slip; it is an English-side typesetting defect only.
questions.stem: A pair of dice is thrown and the sum of the numbers appearing on the dice is observed to be 7. Find the probability that the number 5 has appeared on atleast one die.

The probability that A hits the target is \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) and the probability that B hits it, is \(\dfrac{2}{5}\). If both try to hit the target independently, find the probability that the target is hit.
Find the particular solution of the differential equation \(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = x^2 \cdot e^x\), given \(y(1) = 0\).
Find the general solution of the differential equation \(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = y(\log y - \log x + 1)\).

The two adjacent sides of a parallelogram are represented by vectors \(2\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}\) and \(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}\). Find the unit vector parallel to one of its diagonals. Also, find the area of the parallelogram.

If \(\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}\) and \(\vec{c} = 3\hat{i} + \hat{j}\) are such that the vector \((\vec{a} + \lambda \vec{b})\) is perpendicular to vector \(\vec{c}\), then find the value of \(\lambda\).
Show that the lines : \(\dfrac{1 - x}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{4} = \dfrac{z}{-1}\) and \(\dfrac{x - 4}{3} = \dfrac{2y - 2}{-4} = z - 1\) are coplanar.

questions.subtopic: Area Bounded by a Curve and a Line
questions.stem: Find the area of the region bounded by curve \(4x^2 = y\) and the line \(y = 8x + 12\), using integration.

Find the distance of the point (1, -2, 9) from the point of intersection of the line \(\vec{r} = 4\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 7\hat{k} + \lambda(3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})\) and the plane \(\vec{r} \cdot (\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = 10\).
